title: Restore hearing in OTOF-related deafness with an approved gene therapy

concept.text: Restore auditory signalling in people with biallelic OTOF variants and preserved outer hair-cell function. Otarmeni achieved accelerated approval, with durability and effects on speech development requiring continued verification. Proposed completion test: FDA accelerated approval for genetically confirmed OTOF-associated severe-to-profound hearing loss, based on clinically substantial hearing improvement against untreated natural history, with confirmatory durability and functional follow-up required. Test set by: FDA; its assessment included a 24-patient study, with hearing improvement in 80% of the 20 efficacy-evaluable patients. Reported achieved: FDA granted accelerated approval to lunsotogene parvec-cwha (Otarmeni) on 23 April 2026. Sources given: [FDA Otarmeni approval announcement](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-ever-gene-therapy-treatment-genetic-hearing-loss-under-national-priority-voucher) ; [FDA Otarmeni product and approval record](https://www.fda.gov/vaccines-blood-biologics/otarmeni).

page.title: Gene therapy for OTOF-related deafness
page.definition: A licensed gene therapy improves hearing sensitivity in people with disease-causing variants in both copies of OTOF. This gene encodes otoferlin, a protein that inner hair cells in the cochlea need to transmit sound signals to the auditory nerve. Otarmeni supplies those cells with a working copy of OTOF. Its U.S. licence covers children and adults with genetically confirmed OTOF-related hearing loss exceeding 90 dB hearing level at any frequency, preserved outer hair cell function and no previous cochlear implant in the treated ear.

goal.need: OTOF variants account for 2%–8% of inherited nonsyndromic hearing loss. Hearing aids offer little benefit when inner hair cells cannot pass sound signals to the auditory nerve. Cochlear implants can improve speech perception by stimulating the nerve directly. Restoring the cells’ own signalling gives people who want acoustic hearing another option. Some treated children can hear soft speech without a device. Learning to interpret those sounds can still take time.

statements.body: National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders
statements.quote: Replacing the faulty otoferlin gene with a functioning version could be an approach to restoring hearing in those with otoferlin-related hearing loss.
However, the NAD firmly opposes its use to alter hearing status or eliminate Deaf identity.
statements.context: Standing Our Ground states the association’s position on gene therapy and describes the Deaf community as a linguistic and cultural minority.

completion.title: A regulator authorises a gene therapy for hearing loss caused by biallelic OTOF variants.
completion.criterion: The competent authority in at least one jurisdiction grants marketing authorisation for at least one gene therapy whose approved indication includes hearing loss caused by disease-associated variants in both copies of OTOF. The decision takes effect for the patient population specified in the authorisation. An FDA biologics licence granted through either traditional or accelerated approval qualifies.
completion.set_by: The competent marketing-authorisation authority for the jurisdiction, including FDA in the United States and the European Commission in the European Union.
completion.threshold_quote: FDA approval to market a biologic is granted by issuance of a biologics license.
completion.basis: FDA licensed Otarmeni (lunsotogene parvec-cwha) on 23 April 2026 under accelerated approval. At week 24, 16 of 20 children in the efficacy analysis reached an average hearing threshold of 70 dB HL or less. One child with missing week-24 data counted as a nonresponder. FDA requires 104-week follow-up in at least 30 treated paediatric patients and analyses including at least five newly treated patients aged 16 or older. The postmarketing study must compare hearing, speech and language, global improvement and quality of life with outcomes in comparable untreated patients.

milestones.title: OTOF gene transfer restores reproducible auditory brainstem responses in a deaf animal model.
milestones.criterion: After OTOF gene transfer, sound evokes a reproducible auditory brainstem response in a treated ear in an otherwise deaf OTOF-deficient animal model. For a click stimulus, the threshold is the lowest sound pressure level that evokes a reproducible electrical waveform.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Human Gene Therapy for Rare Diseases, January 2020, section IV: a nonbinding qualitative preclinical recommendation. The OTOF-specific readout is documented by Al-Moyed et al.
milestones.threshold_quote: demonstrate a biological response to the investigational GT product that is similar to the expected response in humans.

milestones.title: Children treated for OTOF-related deafness complete six weeks of toxicity assessment.
milestones.criterion: Children with confirmed biallelic OTOF variants and severe-to-complete hearing loss receive gene therapy and complete the protocol’s six-week assessment for dose-limiting toxicity. Under Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events version 5.0, the qualifying grades are 4 or higher for haematologic toxicity, 3 or higher for non-haematologic toxicity and 2 or higher for aural toxicity.
milestones.set_by: Eye & ENT Hospital of Fudan University, ethics-approved protocol [2022]2022085-1, registered as ChiCTR2200063181; primary safety endpoint published by Lv et al.
milestones.threshold_quote: The primary endpoint was dose-limiting toxicity at 6 weeks after injection.

milestones.title: The week-24 hearing response rate exceeds CHORD’s 2% natural-history benchmark.
milestones.criterion: A child responds if the week-24 behavioural pure-tone threshold averages 70 dB HL or less across 0.5, 1, 2 and 4 kHz. For bilateral treatment, use the better-performing treated ear. The cohort meets the primary efficacy test when a one-sided exact binomial test at α = 0.025 shows that the responder proportion exceeds 2%.
milestones.set_by: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, CHORD protocol DB-OTO-001 (NCT05788536), as reported by the CHORD Study Group in the Statistical Analysis section.
milestones.threshold_quote: a 2% null response was chosen as a conservative upper-limit benchmark

milestones.title: A treated child’s average auditory brainstem response threshold improves by at least 10 dB.
milestones.criterion: In a child with biallelic OTOF deafness, the treated ear’s auditory brainstem response threshold falls by at least 10 dB from baseline, averaged across 0.5, 1, 2 and 4 kHz. The protocol schedules post-treatment hearing assessments at weeks 4, 6, 13 and 26.
milestones.set_by: Eye & ENT Hospital of Fudan University, registered trial ChiCTR2200063181, secondary efficacy assessment.
milestones.threshold_quote: Hearing recovery was defined as a 10 dB reduction in the average ABR threshold

milestones.title: A regulatory review committee recommends marketing approval for an OTOF gene therapy.
milestones.criterion: After evaluating a marketing application, the responsible scientific review committee records a favourable recommendation for a gene therapy to treat hearing loss caused by biallelic OTOF variants.
milestones.set_by: FDA’s biologics review committee in its Summary Basis for Regulatory Action, with an analogous scientific recommendation in the EU centralised procedure.
milestones.threshold_quote: The Review Committee recommends approval of this product.

not_found: No OTOF-specific numerical animal-efficacy cutoff was found in the FDA guidance or approval documents.

results.finding: In 25 treated Otof-knockout mice included in the analysis, reproducible click-evoked auditory brainstem response thresholds ranged from 40 to 60 dB SPL.
results.detail: About two-thirds of injected knockout mice showed neither a detectable response nor evidence of transduction and were classified as non-transduced controls.
results.quote: Acoustic clicks evoked auditory brainstem responses with thresholds of 40–60 dB.

results.finding: Click-evoked auditory brainstem responses returned in 5 of 5 deaf Otof-knockout mice treated after hearing onset.
results.detail: The postnatal day 17 cohort directly demonstrates reversal after hearing onset. A second cohort treated on postnatal day 30 also recovered responses, with near-wild-type thresholds maintained for 20 weeks (n = 3).
results.quote:
ABR recordings 4 wk after injection showed hearing recovery in all of the mice receiving injections on P17 (
n
= 5), with ABR thresholds in response to clicks or tone-burst stimuli remarkably similar to those in wild-type mice

results.finding: Six children treated with AAV1-hOTOF completed the six-week assessment, with zero dose-limiting toxicities.
results.detail: Two grade 3 events of decreased neutrophil count occurred in one child, below the grade 4 threshold for haematologic toxicity.
results.quote:
All 
participants completed follow-up visits up to week 26. No dose-limiting toxicity or serious adverse events occurred.

results.finding: Participant 3, one of six children treated with AAV1-hOTOF, had a greater than 47 dB reduction in average treated-ear ABR threshold at week 26.
results.detail: The paper reports hearing recovery in five children. Participant 1 had only click-evoked ABR at baseline, so that child’s recovery cannot establish a change from a four-frequency baseline.
results.quote:
In participant 3, the average 
ABR threshold was greater than 95 dB at baseline, 60 dB 
at 4 weeks, 63 dB at 6 weeks, 63 dB at 13 weeks, and 
48 dB at 26 weeks (figure C).

results.finding: Two of six children treated with AAV1-hOTOF reached the pure-tone threshold cutoff at week 26.
results.detail: The trial summarized results descriptively. Three children lacked behavioural pure-tone data, so the count should not be read as a CHORD endpoint response rate.
results.quote:
The 
average pure-tone 
audiometry threshold was 71 dB at 4 weeks, 68 dB at 
6 weeks, 55 dB at 13 weeks, and 30 dB at 26 weeks.

results.finding: Among 42 AAV1-hOTOF recipients in a mixed-age trial, zero dose-limiting toxicities were reported within six weeks.
results.detail: The abstract reports grade 3 decreased neutrophil count. The milestone specifies grade 4 or higher for hematologic dose-limiting toxicity.
results.quote: The primary end point was dose-limiting toxicity within 6 weeks. The secondary end point assessed efficacy and adverse events. No dose-limiting toxicities were observed.

results.finding: In the AAV1-hOTOF hearing-recovery group, mean auditory brainstem response threshold was 54 dB nHL at one year (27 treated ears).
results.detail: The baseline and one-year means use different numbers of ears. The age-stratified caption gives sample sizes and describes within-subject changes, with numerical changes absent from the supplied text.
results.quote: Hearing was recovered in 90% of participants treated with AAV1-hOTOF, with gradual and stable improvement in auditory brainstem response threshold from greater than 97 ± 1 dB normalized hearing level at baseline to 54 ± 3, 51 ± 3, 50 ± 3 and 42 ± 5 dB normalized hearing level at 1, 1.5, 2 and 2.5 years

results.finding: After AAV1-hOTOF, mean behavioral threshold in the hearing-recovery group reached 37 dB HL at 2.5 years (7 treated ears).
results.quote: behavioural audiometry improving from greater than 96 ± 3 dB hearing level at baseline to 37 ± 5 dB hearing level at 2.5 years

results.finding: Among 12 children treated with DB-OTO, 67 adverse events occurred or worsened during or after treatment.
results.detail: Continued participation alone does not establish completion of the six-week assessment or whether any events reached the specified toxicity grades.
results.quote: A total of 67 adverse events occurred or worsened during or after treatment, none of which led to discontinued participation in the study.

results.finding: At week 24, 9 of 12 children treated with DB-OTO had a click-evoked ABR at or below 90 dB nHL.
results.detail: The reported result is from week 24. The supplied text gives no ear-level, frequency-specific changes from baseline.
results.quote: a PTA average threshold of 70 dB HL or less at week 24 (primary end point) and an auditory brain-stem response at or below 90 dB nHL (key secondary end point) were found in 9 of the 12 participants

results.finding: At week 24, 9 of 12 children treated with DB-OTO reached an average behavioural PTA threshold of 70 dB HL or less.
results.detail: The count clears the statistical benchmark if the reported responders were classified using the specified four frequencies and the better-performing treated ear after bilateral treatment.
results.quote: a PTA average threshold of 70 dB HL or less at week 24 (primary end point) and an auditory brain-stem response at or below 90 dB nHL (key secondary end point) were found in 9 of the 12 participants (75%; 95% confidence interval, 43 to 95; P = 1.1×10 -13  for both end points).

results.finding: In 24 children treated with Otarmeni for OTOF-related deafness, the shortest reported safety follow-up was 9 weeks.
results.detail: The label reports overall adverse reactions without a six-week dose-limiting toxicity analysis.
results.quote:
The median duration 
of follow-up was 45 weeks (range 9 to 115 weeks) [see Clinical Studies (14)].

results.finding: At week 24, 14 of 20 Otarmeni-treated children met the study’s click ABR endpoint.
results.detail: The click endpoint used a cutoff of 90 dB nHL.

results.finding: At week 24, 16 of 20 Otarmeni-treated children met the prespecified pure-tone hearing threshold.
results.detail: The exact p-value was calculated from the count in Table 2. The label reports a 95% confidence interval of 56% to 94%.

results.finding: In 2026, the FDA granted Otarmeni accelerated approval for eligible children and adults with biallelic OTOF-related hearing loss.
results.quote:
This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on the improvement of hearing 
sensitivity assessed by average pure tone audiometry (PTA) at Week 24 [see Clinical Studies 
(14)].

results.finding: The FDA granted U.S. accelerated approval to one gene therapy, Otarmeni, for biallelic OTOF-related hearing loss.
results.quote:
Effective this date, we have approved your BLA for lunsotogene parvec-cwha (biologic) 
and the associated drug product Administration Kit (device), under accelerated approval

results.finding: After OTOF transfer, 14 deaf Otof−/− mice in the mid-Myo15 group had a mean treated-ear click ABR threshold of 46.07 dB SPL.
results.detail: Auditory brainstem response recovery persisted through 52 weeks after neonatal treatment.
results.quote: the click ABR thresholds in the injected ear were restored to 46.07 ± 1.19 dB

results.finding: Otof gene transfer restored auditory brainstem responses in 27 profoundly deaf mutant mice (p < 0.0001 versus untreated mutants for each treatment group).
results.detail: Recovered thresholds persisted at the last assessment, three months after treatment. Wave I amplitudes remained below control levels.
results.quote: Interestingly, ABRs recorded 3 weeks after injection in treated mice at P2 and P30 revealed hearing thresholds similar to those in control mice

results.finding: The FDA Review Committee reviewed 1 marketing application for Otarmeni and recommended accelerated approval for hearing loss caused by biallelic OTOF variants.
results.detail: The CNPV Review Council unanimously concurred with the recommendation after deliberating on April 17, 2026.
results.quote: Recommended Action: The Review Committee recommends approval of this product.

definition = "A gene therapy licensed by a regulator improves hearing sensitivity in OTOF-related deafness, which is caused by disease-associated variants in both copies of the gene encoding otoferlin, a protein needed for sound transmission from the inner ear to the auditory nerve.
